newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 6.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters

Following the suspension of three investment funds earlier this week after the discovery of irregularities at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, Deutsche Bank, owners of MGAM, says it is considering moving responsibility for its UK unit trust business from London to Frankfurt.
-- CHELSEA FC DIRECTOR GIVES 1 MILLION STG TO LABOUR
Insurance broker Matthew Harding, who has been at the centre of a boardroom struggle to take control of London football club Chelsea, is to make a one million sterling donation to the Labour party.
-- RETAILERS' SURVEY SHOWS BUOYANT HIGH STREET SALES

A business survey from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) shows that high street business conditions are more upbeat than at any time since the last consumer boom of 1988. It finds that two-thirds of retailers reported higher August sales this year compared to 1995, a trend which may concern the Bank of England as its monitors inflationary pressures.
-- GENERATORS IN SCRAMBLE TO BUILD POWER STATIONS

The number of power stations planned for construction is to reach its highest since the electricity generation industry was privatised in 1991. The National Grid group has made 12 applications for gas-fired power stations since March, an expansion which would add over 10 per cent to existing capacity in England and Wales. Industry executives say the level of applications underlines the strong interest of independent generators in the UK market.
-- ENGLAND DEAL SAVES RUGBY'S OLDEST CONTEST

The English Rugby Football Union, the English game's ruling body, has reached agreement with its British Isles counterparts in Scotland, Wales and Ireland over the sharing of television revenues. The deal will ensure the survival of the prestigious Five Nations championship, from which England was expelled in May after unilaterally agreeing an 87.5 million stg deal with satellite broadcaster BSkyB.
-- NATIONAL GRID OPTIMISTIC ON PROFITS PLEA

National Grid, operator of the high voltage transmission system in England and Wales, is hopeful that a meeting on Monday between its executives and industry regulator Professor Stephen Littlechild of Offer has pursuaded Littlechild to modify his original plans to cut up to 1.2 billion stg from the company's profits.
-- AUGUST CAR FIGURES DASH HOPES OF BIG SALES BOOM

Hopes within the UK car industry of a sales boom this year have been dashed after figures revealed that new car registrations in August -- the busiest month of the year for dealers -- rose by just 2.2 per cent, to 479,407. The first seven months of 1996 had seen a 5.5 per cent rise in sales, and there had been hopes the August total match the 500,000 peak achieved in the consumer boom of 1989.
-- ROYAL SUN TO CUT A THIRD OF TOP MANAGERS

Composite insurer Royal & Sun Alliance has predicted it will have lost almost one third of its senior members by the time the recently merged group finishes integrating its businesses. The forecast was made as the group announced its first combined results since the six billion stg merger was completed in July, showing a smaller-than-expected fall in half-year operating profits, from 514 million stg to 450 million stg.
